question.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=4$ for $x\ge 0$ and $z\le 0.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\sqrt{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})^{3}}\,\text{d}V
$$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $2$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/540ae5200e5628d721a64b2ee5ad2b3f0e3f7c3192ccb1f90aeab71abc93f070.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 2,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\sqrt{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})^{3}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\sqrt{{({\rho }^{2})}^{3}} \\  & ={\rho }^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\sqrt{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})^{3}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{3}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\rho }^{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$
